quote: The boy is dead, and he has been dead thirty years.
why: Elowen wrote this letter at least sixteen years ago, so the boy could have been dead only about fourteen years when she wrote it.

quote: The assize is a week and a half off
why: Day 13 to an assize on the 30th is about 17 days. R138 has the DM admit it said 'the twentieth' and 'a week and a half off,' and 'both were mistakes.'

quote: eight guards in the reeds behind you
why: R125 says 'Six guards in grey cloaks' go and 'two more stay behind with the hall'; R127's own hidden note says Pell and six guards. R126 also says 'Eight guards are in reeds or at the road, with Pell.'

quote: Three bandits still stand near you, two with scimitars and two behind with crossbows.
why: Three versus two plus two. Four bandits are left (1, 2, 3, 5).

quote: They're thirty paces off now and closing fast.
why: R132 said 'The guards are twenty paces off and running' and R131 said they 'will reach the culvert this round'. The guards are 'a round away' for five rounds, and the distance goes up from 20 to 30 paces.

quote: eight guards in front of him
why: Only Pell and six guards exist (R133: 'Pell... with six grey cloaks'; the same reply ends 'Pell and six guards hold the line'). Wren bluffed 'eight crossbows' but the DM narrates it as fact, and again in R135.

quote: with spears flying over the tailboard
why: R125 and R133 have the guards with crossbows and short swords ('crossbows already up'); now they fight with spears and thrown spears.

quote: Eight crossbows are on him.
why: Six guards plus Pell; see R134. Several of them have already thrown their spears.

quote: My grandsire Aldous gave it to the Lantern-Bearer
why: R135 Ansel: 'Your mother took the lamp from me, and I have wanted it back for sixteen years.' It was given by his grandsire, not taken from him.

quote: a camp under a grey sky
why: The same reply ends 'the first stars are coming out over the flats'.

quote: I said Thornhallow was a day's ride from the causeway. It isn't.
why: R140 told the player 'It's a day's ride to Thornhallow' and R139 had Pell agree to go there first. The trip becomes two more days after the player built a plan on it.

quote: your Perception comes up an 11 only
why: The roll shown is 1d20 [10] + 2 = 12.

quote: Two riders go a mile ahead and two a mile behind, and a third goes back to Saltmarsh
why: R139: Pell sent two of his guards back to Saltmarsh, which leaves 4 of the original 6. Five riders are used here, leaving Pell alone with five prisoners. R152 and R153 then send three more riders.

quote: All three of you at the gate are looking at the barn now
why: Only Wren and Kit are at the gate (Kit went to wake Pell and came back).

quote: he has missed you four times running
why: Sparrow's shots at Wren in this fight: R147, R148, R149. That is three (R148 a nat 1).

quote: Bought a hack off the miller at Dunnock Ford yesterday at dusk
why: Sparrow was at the farm barn fight at 10:30 PM on Day 16 (Kit cut him for 10), so he could not have bought a horse at dusk, and the drover describes the stiff arm the wound caused later. The timeline is impossible, and the Osric lead rests on it.

quote: But I've six spears, a cellar with one door
why: Pell started with six guards (R134); two were sent to Saltmarsh in R139 and Wren is taking two more. R160 still has 'six tired guards' arriving.

quote: Five days there and five back
why: R141: Saltmarsh to Marrowford is four days and Thornhallow lies a day below Marrowford, so about three days. The ten-day figure (repeated in R166 as 'It's five days to Saltmarsh') has no basis, and a lone rider would be faster than a wagon.

quote: Pell's wagon will arrive in a day or two.
why: R162 has Edric holding Ansel at Thornhallow until he rides on the 29th. R165 ('Pell's guards will bring the prisoners behind you'), R172 and R173 ('Pell's wagon with Corvin and Ansel's shadow is still on the road behind') keep the prisoners on the road.

quote: To hold at Sedge Creek until the 24th, for the lamp.
why: Tam Rudd (R152): Harrow was paid half and would wait only 'till the dawn ebb the day after tomorrow' (Day 18), then sail north. Now he is paid in full and holds until Day 24.

quote: Eleven years ago a man who signed himself Aldous wrote to him
why: Hale entered Edric's household 'twelve years ago, a little more' on Oake's recommendation (R160), and the letter in his box is 'twelve years old' (R164). Hale cannot have been sent in response to a letter written a year later.

quote: Oake's own hand on today's statement is upright and cramped
why: R173: 'You write it down, and Lyle reads it back, and he signs it.' Wren wrote the statement; Oake only signed it.

quote: Kit is forty feet or so up the hedge
why: R177 and R179 had Kit 'forty paces' (about 120 ft) behind Wren.
